theory.overview: Profiling measures program performance to identify bottlenecks. Tools like CPU profilers, memory profilers, and flame graphs reveal where time is spent and memory is allocated. Understanding profiling helps optimize hot paths and reduce resource usage.

sections.title: Sampling vs Instrumentation
sections.content: Sampling periodically interrupts the program to see what's running (low overhead, statistical). Instrumentation adds code to track execution (precise, higher overhead).

sections.title: Flame Graphs
sections.content: Visual representation of call stacks. The x-axis is population (not time), y-axis is stack depth. Wide bars indicate hot paths worth optimizing.

examples.explanation: Wide bars = functions consuming most CPU time

sections.title: Hardware Counters
sections.content: CPU performance counters measure cache misses, branch mispredictions, cycles per instruction, and other low-level metrics. These reveal micro-architectural bottlenecks.

sections.title: Memory Profiling
sections.content: Track allocations, detect leaks, identify fragmentation. Tools like Valgrind, AddressSanitizer, and heap profilers show where memory is consumed and if it's properly freed.

keyConcepts.name: Cache Miss
keyConcepts.description: Data not in CPU cache, causes delay

steps.title: Setting Up Profiling
steps.content: Choose appropriate profiler for your needs: perf (Linux), Instruments (macOS), VTune (Intel), or language-specific tools. Compile with debug symbols for accurate source mapping.

steps.title: Capturing Data
steps.content: Run representative workloads. Sampling profilers need enough samples for statistical significance. Instrumentation may need release builds with frame pointers preserved.

steps.title: Analyzing Results
steps.content: Identify hot functions (most time spent), call patterns (who calls hot functions), and opportunity areas (functions consuming more time than expected).

practiceProblems.title: Sampling Accuracy
practiceProblems.description: A function runs for 1ms in a 10-second execution. With 1000 samples, will it appear?
practiceProblems.solution: Expected 0.1 samples (1ms/10000ms * 1000). It might not appear or appear once. Short-running functions may be invisible to sampling.

practiceProblems.title: Cache Miss Profile
practiceProblems.description: A loop has high L1 cache miss rate. What's a likely cause?
practiceProblems.solution: Strided access pattern or data structure layout. Solutions: cache blocking/tiling, structure of arrays instead of array of structures, prefetching.

minigame.title: Performance Detective
minigame.description: Analyze profile data to identify and fix performance bottlenecks
